Similarly D_{S_j}Vfield=(D_{S_j}Lfield)[T]. Apply M007 to ũ at (x0,tau), using F001's C² regularity. Symmetry of its second derivative makes these expressions equal. Thus the mixed derivative needed in the energy calculation is D_T Wfield_j=D_{S_j}Vfield at (x0,tau).

Apply M005 to the time curve r↦Vfield(x0,r) at tau, whose derivative is Afield(x0,tau), and for each j to r↦Wfield_j(x0,r), whose derivative is D_T Wfield_j(x0,tau). These derivatives follow from F001 and the directional definitions. Differentiate the finite sum in D011 and substitute F002. This yields ∂_t e(x0,tau)=2⟨Vfield,Afield⟩(x0,tau)+2Σ_j⟨Wfield_j,D_{S_j}Vfield⟩(x0,tau).

For each j apply M006 on Xn×ℝ to f=Vfield, g=Wfield_j, direction S_j at (x0,tau). Both functions are differentiable there by F001. D012 identifies their inner product with g_j on the positive-time neighborhood, and Bfield_j=D_{S_j}Wfield_j. The product rule gives ∂_{x_j}g_j(x0,tau)=⟨Vfield(x0,tau),Bfield_j(x0,tau)⟩+⟨D_{S_j}Vfield(x0,tau),Wfield_j(x0,tau)⟩.

Subtract twice the finite sum of F004 from F003. Symmetry of the real inner product cancels the terms containing D_{S_j}Vfield. Bilinearity combines the remaining terms into 2⟨Vfield,Afield-Σ_j Bfield_j⟩(x0,tau). The identifications in the declarations make this 2⟨u_t,u_tt-Σ_j∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩(x0,tau), which is zero by the second clause of N001. Hence ∂_t e=2Σ_j∂_{x_j}g_j at this point, with exactly the factor 2. Universal introduction over arbitrary x0 and positive tau proves the claimed output.

argument.text: Fix tau>0 and define Uwin,Fpar,Dpar as declared. By N002, Fpar and Dpar are jointly continuous on Uwin×Xn after swapping the two coordinates. Smoothness of e gives, for every x∈Xn and r∈Uwin, HasDerivAt (s↦Fpar(s)(x)) Dpar(r)(x) r: the affine time inclusion has derivative T, so D010 identifies its chain-rule derivative with ∂_t e. Every r in Uwin is positive. N004 makes Fpar(r) and Dpar(r) integrable for every such r, and integrability implies almost everywhere strong measurability. In particular Fpar(tau) is integrable and Dpar(tau) is almost everywhere strongly measurable. Uwin is an open neighborhood of tau, so measurability of Fpar(r) holds eventually at tau.

produces.statement: Fpar and Dpar are jointly continuous on Uwin×Xn; for every x∈Xn and r∈Uwin the time curve has derivative Dpar(r)(x) at r. Fpar(r) and Dpar(r) are integrable and almost everywhere strongly measurable for every r∈Uwin. Uwin is a neighborhood of tau.

argument.text: Choose Cwin by N002 at tau; throughout Uwin, both Fpar and Dpar vanish outside this same compact set. Compact subsets of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space are bounded. Thus the absolute values of all finitely many coordinates on Cwin have a finite common bound. Enlarging that bound by 1 gives a positive radius with Cwin contained in its closed coordinate cube; if Cwin is empty, any positive radius suffices.

produces.statement: Cwin is compact, Fpar(r)(x)=Dpar(r)(x)=0 for every r∈Uwin and x∉Cwin, and there exists rho>0 with Cwin⊂[-rho,rho]^n.

argument.text: Choose rho by F002 and define Qbox and Lwin. Each closed bounded coordinate interval is compact; their finite product Qbox is compact in Xn. The interval Lwin is compact and lies in Uwin, since tau>0 gives tau/2<3tau/4≤5tau/4<3tau/2. Thus Lwin×Qbox is compact. By F001, the real function (r,x)↦|Dpar(r)(x)| is continuous on this compact set. Its continuous image is bounded, so a nonnegative real bound exists (also when the set is empty).

produces.statement: Qbox is compact, Cwin⊂Qbox, Lwin⊂Uwin, and there exists beta≥0 such that |Dpar(r)(x)|≤beta for every r∈Lwin and x∈Qbox.

argument.text: Choose beta by F003, and define bdom and Iwin. The closed cube Qbox is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure (2rho)^n. The indicator multiple bdom is measurable and its absolute integral is beta(2rho)^n<∞, so bdom is integrable. The interval Iwin is an open neighborhood of tau and is contained in Lwin and Uwin. For x∈Qbox and r∈Iwin, F003 gives |Dpar(r)(x)|≤beta=bdom(x). For x∉Qbox, the inclusion Cwin⊂Qbox implies x∉Cwin, so F002 gives Dpar(r)(x)=0=bdom(x). Thus the bound holds for every x and every r∈Iwin, which also implies the single almost-everywhere assertion with all r in this same neighborhood. F001 supplies the time derivative for every x and every r∈Iwin.

produces.statement: Iwin is a neighborhood of tau contained in Uwin. bdom is Lebesgue integrable, and for every x∈Xn and every r∈Iwin, |Dpar(r)(x)|≤bdom(x) and HasDerivAt (s↦Fpar(s)(x)) Dpar(r)(x) r.

argument.text: Apply M002 with spatial measure dx, F=Fpar, D=Dpar, base time tau, neighborhood Iwin and bound bdom. F001 gives eventual section measurability, base integrability and derivative-section measurability; F004 gives the neighborhood, the integrable bound and both universally quantified pointwise conditions, hence their almost-everywhere forms. The theorem concludes integrability of Dpar(tau) and HasDerivAt (r↦∫_{Xn}Fpar(r)(x) dx) (∫_{Xn}Dpar(tau)(x) dx) tau.

By D011 and D013, the integral time function in F005 is exactly the total representation of E, and its restriction to positive times is the desired energy. The section integrability already instantiated in F001 ensures these are finite Lebesgue integrals for times in Uwin, a neighborhood of tau. Dpar(tau)(x)=∂_t e(x,tau) since tau>0. Restriction to the open positive-time domain preserves this derivative, so F005 gives every clause of the claimed output for this tau. The conclusion contains none of Cwin,rho,beta or the auxiliary windows; eliminate their witnesses and universally quantify tau. No behavior at zero is asserted.

argument.text: Fix tau>0 and a coordinate j0 and define gspace. N002 makes gspace smooth by restriction along the affine map x↦(x,tau), hence globally C¹. Its topological support is compact: N002 at center time tau contains it in a compact spatial set, and tsupport is closed. The same affine inclusion has derivative h↦(h,0). Therefore by the chain rule, for every x∈Xn, Dgspace(x)[b_{j0}]=∂_{x_{j0}}g_{j0}(x,tau), with exactly the directional interpretation D006–D010. These facts require no hypotheses beyond N002's smoothness and support statements.

argument.text: Apply E004 with g=gspace and the constant spatial vector v=b_{j0}. F001 verifies its C¹ and compact-support premises. It gives integrability of Dgspace(·)[b_{j0}] and its zero integral. Using F001's pointwise derivative identification yields ∫_{Xn}∂_{x_{j0}}g_{j0}(x,tau) dx=0. The result is independent of the notation gspace; since j0 was arbitrary, this proves the zero integral for every coordinate.

At time tau, N003 is the pointwise equality ∂_t e(x,tau)=2Σ_j∂_{x_j}g_j(x,tau). N004 supplies integrability of the left side and of each derivative on the right. Linearity of the Lebesgue integral for finite sums and real scalar multiplication therefore applies and gives ∫_{Xn}∂_t e(x,tau) dx=2Σ_j∫_{Xn}∂_{x_j}g_j(x,tau) dx=0 by F002. This is finite integral linearity, so no infinite interchange is involved. Since tau>0 was arbitrary, universal introduction proves the claimed output.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary tau>0. N004 states that e(·,tau) is Lebesgue integrable, so D013's E(tau) is the finite actual integral required by the target. N005 gives a derivative of E at tau with value ∫_{Xn}∂_t e(x,tau) dx. N006 identifies precisely this integral as zero. Substitution therefore gives HasDerivAt E 0 tau on the open positive-time domain. By the definition and uniqueness of a derivative this entails differentiability there and E'(tau)=0. The formula for e in D011 is |u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|², and D010 gives the stated Frobenius and componentwise Laplacian normalizations, with no factor 1/2. Since tau>0 was arbitrary this is all clauses of the target, including integrability at every positive time and no assertion at time zero.
